note: Run covering 2026-08-09 -> 2026-08-10, executed 09:15 UTC Monday pre-market. 11 lines appended (9 bot dailies, 1 crypto trade_event, 1 sentinel daily). 13 new fills audited, all XRP-USD, ALL CLEAN - no SIM-INTEGRITY ALERT. There has been no US equity session since the 2026-08-07 close, so eight books are logged with driver 'unknown' and an explicit statement that the market was shut, rather than a manufactured cause. Two root causes were found in the workflow logs this run and both are recorded in the evidence fields verbatim: the rebase-conflict poisoning that produces the ~362-minute blackouts, and the xAI HTTP 403 credit exhaustion that has frozen the Grok watcher for 70.4 hours.
driver_note: Only one bot had a live day, so the shape barely moved, but the move it made is the point. 'technical' went 11-14 to 11-16 and is now decisively the worst-scoring driver in the fleet. 'technical' in this ledger is overwhelmingly one thing - the crypto bot's signal-flip rule - and today produced the cleanest evidence yet that it loses on COST rather than on direction: across the four round trips scored this run the rule's price selection made +15.46 gross and the book still finished -5.73 after 21.19 of fees. A driver bucket that is right about price and wrong about money is exactly the case where a naive win/loss tally would mislead, so it is worth stating explicitly. 'unknown' flat count jumps 56 to 64 purely because eight closed-market days were logged honestly instead of being attributed to a cause. news_idiosyncratic stays the standout at 7-1 on a small sample and I keep holding it to a citation every time. hype_sentiment stays 7-10, or 6-11 once the SOUN phantom profit is stripped out.
beta_alpha_note: alpha 33-23 after the crypto loss landed in the alpha bucket again. The label keeps flattering the fleet: it is driven by single-asset all-in books (hunter in SLV, hype in one name, crypto in one coin) where any divergence from a broad benchmark reads as alpha by construction. Crypto remains the clean counter-example - it diverged from its benchmark by 0.51pp on the day and every basis point of that divergence was fees, which is divergence without skill. The n/a flat count now dominates the table at 87, which is an honest artefact of reviewing a mostly-equity fleet across a long market closure and should not be read as the fleet being idle.
